page: Amazon Web Services m8g.12xlarge is a general-purpose cloud server instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the AWS Graviton4 processor family. Featuring the 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 microarchitecture, this server provides 48 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.8 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. It is equipped with 64 KB L1 data cache per core, 2 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 192.0 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per physical core. The instance includes 22 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. It does not bundle local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached storage architectures for persistence.

Benchmark results show exceptional memory throughput and multi-threaded processing density. The instance achieves top-tier results in uncached large-block memory read bandwidth at 404.77 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 210.23 GB/sec, matching its high-ranking PassMark memory score of 3356.66. Compute scaling across the 48 dedicated cores produces a top-tier Geekbench multi-core score of 23,515.0 and Clang software compilation throughput of 71,715.0. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and stress-ng multi-core tests also place in the upper quartile. While single-threaded performance in stress-ng and Geekbench lands within the median range, memory and parallel throughput metrics remain distinct strengths.

The absence of local scratch disks and dedicated vector accelerator flags represents an architectural tradeoff, making the platform reliant on remote storage latency and CPU-bound math instructions. Even so, the 48 independent ARM physical cores achieve high resource density and power efficiency compared to simultaneous-multithreading architectures, maximizing operational throughput per allocated core for large deployments.

Amazon Web Services m8g.12xlarge is suited for software build farms, high-concurrency microservices, static web serving, enterprise databases, and in-memory caches. Its top-tier scores in static web serving throughput and database operations align directly with memory-intensive and parallel execution workloads.
